gen-dafont-true-north-noto-serif: Noto Serif reads like a classic serif with a prominent x-height and a gentle swing between full and slim strokes. But True North, stocky and contemporary, keeps the page from getting too polite, and a long read stays easy.
gen-dafont-vcr-osd-mono-fs-hind: Lo-fi and retro-tech, with towering fixed-width letters in a steady weight. Hind follows in sans-serif, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals, so the code-style heading gets a quiet, straightforward partner underneath.
gen-dafont-vcr-osd-mono-fs-technor: Technor glows like neon tubing, one steady line thickness with little height difference between cases and wide-open bowls. Its cool geometry against the fixed-width, towering VCR OSD Mono is the real hook: two machine-made voices, one lo-fi and one sleek.
gen-dafont-venera-fs-bespoke-serif: Venera spaces its letters so wide that every word looks thinly scattered, clean and modern in feel. Bespoke Serif settles in below with a text serif's dignified, authoritative thick-and-thin strokes.
gen-dafont-venera-fs-sentient: Sophisticated is the mood Sentient brings, with pinched apertures and a subtle pen-like swell in its bowls. Venera, modern and scattered across the line, gives that serif plenty of space to settle against its own low-contrast, widely spaced letters.
gen-dafont-verve-fs-hind: Verve sets heavy stems beside hair-thin strokes, with bowls that nearly seal shut. Hind opens its letters back up, a plain sans whose pen pressure holds steady from the first letter to the last.
gen-dafont-visitor-fs-gambetta: Nostalgic and digital, Visitor pulls its strokes like solder, with gaping e mouths and short ascenders above big bowls. Gambetta's bookish text serif, with weight that shifts noticeably but never dramatically, is the counterweight.
gen-dafont-visitor-lora: Lora brings a literary softness to the page. Visitor's pixel-like strokes have no thick and thin parts at all, while Lora's modest hairline thinning at the curves feels like hand-drawn ink beside them.
gen-dafont-visitor-noto-serif: Visitor draws nostalgic, digital letters with a constant-width line. Noto Serif then carries the text in a serif with a prominent x-height, its fuller stems and slimmer links making a long stretch feel literary and easy to follow.
